study type: Experimental research (animal study) with a posttest only control group design
exposure: Standard feed + iron 1.8 mg/200gBW and folic acid 0.0023 mg/200gBW
Standard feed + iron 3.6 mg/200gBW and folic acid 0.0045 mg/200gBW
Standard feed + iron 5.4 mg/200gBW and folic acid 0.0068 mg/200gBW
cohort: The study included 20 pregnant rats, randomly divided into 4 groups for 20 days of treatment.
finding: Iron and folate supplementation during pregnancy significantly decreased levels of MDA, glucose, creatinine, and maternal body weight, while increasing the average number and fetal weight of offspring, indicating reduced oxidative stress and improved pregnancy outcomes.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome variable for offspring.
